item.text:
**6B.2 Assessment**
Mostly no. There is solid evidence of targeted humanitarian and sectoral support, but not of a broad 2024 improvement in ordinary people’s access to health, education, WASH, housing, food security, and social protection. The strongest positives are partner-led and crisis-specific; the strongest negatives show repression, falling real welfare, and worsening poverty/inequality.

**Accepted Claims**
- **[World Bank Helps Bangladesh Provide Basic Services, Opportunities, and Build Resilience for Displaced Rohingya and Host Communities](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co)** | World Bank | May 28, 2024 | Claim: Bangladesh and partners funded health, nutrition, education, water, shelters, livelihood support, and GBV prevention for Rohingya and host communities. This is the strongest positive evidence for 6B.2, but it is narrowly targeted and heavily partner-financed. | QIDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10

- **[UNICEF and Japan join hands to improve the well-being of Bangladeshi and Rohingya children living in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasan Char](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/262180-unicef-and-japan-join-hands-improve-the-well-being-of-bangladeshi-and-rohingya-children-living)** | United Nations in Bangladesh | March 3, 2024 | Claim: UNICEF reported expanded services for Rohingya children, women, and host communities, including education, WASH, health, and nutrition. Positive, but humanitarian delivery is not the same as a nationwide rise in access under Hasina. | QIDs: 6B.2, 5B.8, 5B.10

- **[Advancing Healthcare Excellence: WHO's Role in Developing the First National Medical Education Strategy in Bangladesh!](https://www.who.int/bangladesh/news/detail/04-03-2024-advancing-healthcare-excellence-who-s-role-in-developing-the-first-national-medical-education-strategy-in-bangladesh)** | WHO Bangladesh | March 4, 2024 | Claim: the health ministry, with WHO support, launched Bangladesh’s first national medical education strategy to improve curriculum, accreditation, faculty development, and digital transformation. This is a real positive for health-system access and quality. | QIDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.10

- **[UNFPA Bangladesh Annual Report 2024](https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024)** | UNFPA Bangladesh | 2024 | Claim: UNFPA delivered targeted reproductive-health, GBV, and cash-support services to women, girls, indigenous communities, transgender people, sex workers, and disaster-affected areas. This shows concrete access gains for vulnerable groups, but again it is partner-led and not strong proof of broad national improvement. | QIDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **[Bangladesh - Cash Transfer Modernization Project: Improving Transparency and Efficiency of Safety Nets](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099739201032424234)** | World Bank | January 1, 2024 | Claim: Bangladesh already had cash-transfer programs aimed at the poorest and most socially excluded, including widows, older people, and disabled people. This is limited positive background for social protection, but it also implies coverage and delivery still needed modernization. | QIDs: 6B.2, 5B.8, 5B.10

- **[Bangladesh: Türk decries government crackdown, urges respect for international human rights standards](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights)** | United Nations / OHCHR | July 26, 2024 | Claim: more than 170 people were reported killed, some injured people were denied medical care, and the UN said there was no effort to protect people from attacks by groups affiliated with the government. This is strong negative evidence that basic safety and welfare access collapsed during the July crisis. | QIDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.7

- **[Bangladesh: Repression, Security Force Abuses Discredit Elections](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections)** | Human Rights Watch | January 11, 2024 | Claim: authorities arrested critics and used repression and violence before the election. This does not directly concern schools or clinics, but it shows the state was prioritizing control over welfare and civic access. | QIDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.1

- **[Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024)** | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: minorities and refugees, especially Rohingya, faced discrimination and insecure access to health care, employment, and education, alongside punitive camp policies and broad corruption. This is direct evidence against equitable access to basic services across groups. | QIDs: 6B.2, 5B.8, 6B.1, 5B.10

- **[Macro Poverty Outlook for Bangladesh: October 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099659510152422672)** | World Bank | October 1, 2024 | Claim: extreme poverty was projected to rise and inequality to widen by more than one Gini point, with jobs and revenue mobilization still weak. That undercuts any claim that access to basic welfare improved broadly in 2024. | QIDs: 6B.2, 5B.8, 5B.9, 5B.10

**Search Gap**
- I did not find strong national-level evidence that Hasina’s government broadly improved access to housing or food security for the general population in 2024.
- The positive evidence is concentrated in humanitarian programs for Rohingya/host communities, targeted social protection, and sectoral health reform, not in economy-wide access gains.
- The negative evidence is stronger on distributional and crisis outcomes than on headline service expansion.
